Why Join ORC?

The Right Work. The Right People. The Right Culture.

Right of Way is where infrastructure meets innovation—shaping roads, utilities, and communities for the future. At ORC, we offer more than a job—we offer purpose, stability, and growth. You’ll join a team that values collaboration, workplace flexibility, and long-term opportunity.

What You’ll Do

Produce maps, exhibits, and figures supporting right of way projects
Create and maintain parcel data, project layers, and geodatabase edits
Perform data entry, cleanup, and quality checks across GIS datasets
Respond to map and data requests from agents, project managers, and clients
Help maintain templates, symbology, and data standards
Perform general tasks that keep project mapping moving

We’re Looking for Someone Who

Is organized, analytical, and detail-oriented — clean data and clean maps matter here
Works efficiently under tight deadlines and keeps multiple priorities moving
Communicates clearly and professionally — with project teams and clients
Enjoys turning project needs into clear, usable maps and data
Brings a strong service mindset to every project team interaction
Picks up new systems and software quickly

Minimum Requirements

Proficiency with Esri ArcGIS (ArcGIS Pro)
Working knowledge of geodatabases and GIS data management
Proficient with MS Office Suite — specifically Excel, Word, and Outlook

Where You Fit

This posting covers GIS Technician levels 1–3, and the pay range shown reflects the full span across all three levels — not the range for any single level.

Every candidate is assessed and evaluated during the hiring process to determine their level based on factors, such as training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs, and market demands. Your offer will reflect the level that best matches your experience.

GIS Technician 1 — $42,443 – $52,088 | Minimum of 1 year of GIS experience using ArcGIS
GIS Technician 2 — $47,966 – $58,834 | Minimum of 3 years of GIS experience using ArcGIS
GIS Technician 3 — $55,200 – $67,669 | Minimum of 6 years of GIS experience using ArcGIS

Relocation and per diem are not provided.

Bonus Points
if you have experience within the Right of Way industry. Or if you have experience with legacy easement mapping or metes and bounds.

What We Offer

Medical, dental, and vision coverage
401(k) with company match, plus disability coverage
Paid time off, sick time, and paid holidays
Tuition reimbursement and paid professional development
ClassPass and Breethe memberships
Recognition programs and real room to grow

That’s the quick version — learn more about benefits at ORC.

Ready to Apply?

Make your mark on projects that matter. Apply now to join a supportive team that invests in your future.

Employees will spend prolonged periods sitting and performing computer-based tasks, including typing, data entry, and virtual communication, while also regularly traveling to landowner properties, project sites, and government facilities, some of which may be in rural or remote locations with limited accessibility. About The Job

We have a vacancy for a researcher at the Department of Psychology in the research group for Citizens, Environment and Safety for 2 years.

The Position Combines Work In Three Externally Funded Projects

The HARMONI project aims to develop a comprehensive knowledge toolbox for hybrid products that combine the benefits of cultivated and plant-based meat alternatives, enabling the creation of appealing new food concepts and expanding future food choices. To achieve this, HARMONI brings together a consortium of Cellular Agriculture and Bioprocess Engineering (Technical University of Munich), Meat Science, Cultivated Muscle Cells and Nutrition (Aarhus University), Material Science and Microbial Systems (Katholieke Universiteit Leuven), Sustainable Food Systems (University of Helsinki), and Environmental and Consumer Psychology (NTNU), complemented by leading industrial partners. The part of NTNU is to study consumer perceptions of such products with focus group interviews, experiments and surveys. Data is likely collected in Norway, Germany, Belgium, and Finnland.
The cells4energy project is a real-world laboratory for 100% renewable energy systems. At its core lies the systemic energy cell approach, where locally generated renewable energy is intelligently stored, utilized, and interconnected with other cells. Through digital technologies and innovative business models, we test in real-world environments how a flexible, resilient, and scalable energy supply can be achieved for the future. The task for NTNU in this project is to implement and analyse the results from an automatized internet-based intervention platform to motivate energy saving. Data will be collected in Austria.
The SaferClay project is a research project focusing on developing methods to assess changes in quick clay landslide risk with time. SAFERCLAY will provide a new approach for adapted and sustainable risk management for living and building in quick clay areas, including recommendations to ensure both public and environmental safety. NTNUs task in this project is analysing perceptions of quick clay and its effects on behaviour in different stakeholder groups. A survey has been designed and is currently implemented in Norway.

What binds the work in all three projects together is the focus on collecting citizen / stakeholder perceptions on novel products, risk factors, and behaviour interventions. In all three projects, these will primarily be studied with quantitative methods, thus excellent knowledge of quantitative analysis methods, data curation and handling, as well as designing research and surveys is essential.

Your immediate leader is the head of department.

Duties of the position

Designing surveys, experiments and qualitative interviews with the respective project groups
Implementation of data collections (in cells4energy coordinated with an external technology provider for the internet platform)
Data cleaning and curation
Data analyses (mainly quantitative, but also qualitatitve)
Preparation of research papers based on the analyses
Feedback and coordination with the research partners

Required Selection Criteria

A finished degree or PhD in psychology with a specialization in environmental psychology, social psychology, behavioural psychology or closely related fields
Excellent skills in data management, curation and complex statistical analysis (e.g. structural equation modelling)
Experience in empirical work in the field
Good written and oral English skills

Preferred Selection Criteria

Experience with work in interdisciplinary fields
Experience with project management
Ability to communicate in at least one of the languages data in the different projects will be collected in (Norwegian, German, Finnish, Flemish, French) in addition to English
Experience with qualitative work

Personal characteristics

Flexibility
Ability to structure your work and handle three projects at the same time
Openness for collaboration with other disciplines and practice partners

We offer

exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment
an open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues
favourable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
employee benefits

Salary and conditions

As a researcher (code 1109) you are normally paid from gross NOK 633 400 per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The position is subject to external funding.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU.

After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

About The Application

Your application and supporting documentation must be in English.

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note:
the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your Application Must Include

CV, diplomas, and certificates
A motivation letter (max 2 pages) outlining your motivation and fit for the position
Academic works – published or unpublished – that you wish to be considered during assessment of your application (up to 5 items)
A description of the scientific/artistic works you consider most relevant, which you particularly wish to be factored into the assessment
A complete publication list
Details of projects for which you have served as project manager or had a significant position in, including information on financing, duration, and scope
Names and contact information for three relevant referees

It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for documentation of your competence.

Joint work will also be considered. If it is difficult to identify your specific input to a joint project, you must include evidence of your contributions.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

NTNU is obliged by the evaluation criteria for research quality in accordance with The San Fransisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and The obligations in the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment ( CoARA) on responsible assessment of research and recognition of a wider range of academic contributions to science and society. This means that we will pay particular attention to the quality and academic range demonstrated by your scientific work to date. We will also pay attention to research leadership and participation in research projects. Your scientific work from the last five years will be given the most weight.

Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview.

General information

Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality.

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Permit Writer
(Environmental Specialist 4) within the Water Resources Program. (WR)

Location:

Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is required to be in the office 2 days each week, on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by October 11, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will have the exciting opportunity to implement Washington Water Law. You will be responsible for managing, processing, evaluating, and drafting support documents for water right decisions. This includes completing investigations by researching, collecting, and analyzing technical data and other information to support water right decisions. You will have the opportunity to identify issues and find possible solutions. You will get to interact with other government agencies, municipalities, and citizens that are looking for water for their projects or homes. There is also an opportunity to let your GIS and mapping skills shine. We are looking for people that want to make a difference, enjoy being part of a team, and are willing to learn.

What You Will Do

Recommend and process water right decisions.
Conduct investigations and technical reviews to support decisions.
Evaluate projects for feasibility, compliance with laws, regulations, and policies.
Work with other local and state government agencies and Tribes regarding Washington water law.
Respond to inquiries from water right applicants, their consultants, other agency staff and the public.
Develop maps and locate water rights using GIS and web mapping tools and software.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Nine years
of combined education and/or experience performing related to the duties of the position, that includes the following:

Experience collecting, researching, and analyzing complex hydrologic or hydrogeologic data to support technical evaluations and regulatory decisions.
Ability to apply scientific, hydrologic, or hydrogeologic findings and/or principles to permitting related decisions.
Demonstrated skill in preparing technical written reports that summarize analyses, findings, and defensible recommendations for permitting decisions.
Ability to conduct and interpret field investigations under the oversight of a licensed hydrogeologist, including groundwater and surface water related analyses.
Experience reviewing proposed water related projects for legal, technical, and policy compliance.
Strong communication and customer service skills, with the ability to interact professionally with applicants, consultants, tribal governments, partner agencies, and the public.

Ability to mentor and support junior staff, collaborate on statewide workgroups, and independently manage workload priorities in a regulatory environment.

About Cdphe

At the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, we are charged with protecting Colorado’s health and

environment – a responsibility that affects every person and every community in the state. CDPHE is distinctive because we bring public health and environmental protection together under one agency, recognizing that healthy people depend on healthy places. Our teams prevent diseases and injury, respond to emergencies ranging from E.coli outbreaks to global pandemics, reduce air pollution, protect water quality, regulate health facilities, manage environmental hazards, perform advanced laboratory testing, provide birth and death records, and implement health promoting programs. We turn science and data into action, set statewide standards, and work alongside local public health agencies and community partners to meet Colorado’s most pressing health and environmental challenges. Working at CDPHE means applying your expertise to complex, consequential work that can improve lives across the state.

Our mission captures this broad portfolio of work: to advance Colorado’s health and protect the places we live, learn, work, and play. Our vision is a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations can thrive. Achieving the mission and vision takes bold action, talented people, broad partnerships, and a commitment to serving every Coloradan.

Important Information

This position will have hybrid workplace options available but will still be required to report to the listed address at the discretion of the supervisor and based on business needs.
The referral list generated by this position announcement may be used to fill multiple position vacancies and may be extended.

CDPHE offers:

CDPHE offers a comprehensive benefits package and the opportunity to build a meaningful career in public service. Benefits include:

Medical and dental plans.
Colorado PERA retirement options, including defined benefit plan or defined contribution plan.
Optional 401(K) and 457 retirement plans.
Employer-paid life insurance.

11 paid holidays per year and generous paid time off.
Free parking and access to RTD bus lines.
Tuition assistance.
Employee wellness programs.
Professional development opportunities.
Career opportunities throughout Colorado state government.

Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program. For more information, go to: https://studentloans.gov/myDirectLoan/pslfFlow.action#!/pslf/launch

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Toxicology and Risk Assessment (TARA) Program is under the direction of the Division of Environmental Health and Sustainability Deputy Director and exists to provide epidemiologic research, surveillance data, toxicology and health risk assessment assistance, and consultation to CDPHE management, divisions and programmatic units; federal and local public health and environmental agencies and officials; and businesses and the public. Our programs span the topics of exposure to toxic substances (e.g., lead, mercury, carbon monoxide, and pesticides), cancer clusters, oil and

gas health impacts, and more.

TARA responds to community concerns about environmental exposures and disease clusters. Staff members provide expertise and oversight for state and community-based environmental health research, health surveillance, and biomonitoring.

The Regulatory Toxicology Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. The Regulatory Toxicology Workgroup conducts health risk investigations and evaluates environmental exposures, hazards and health status of communities. The purpose of this workgroup is to (1) provide statewide consultation to the department's environmental programs other state agencies federal agencies (US EPA, ATSDR) local public health departments, and the general public and (2) conduct public health assessment to identify potential impacts from environmental chemical exposures. The work unit is responsible for reviewing, interpreting and presenting on the toxicological properties of chemicals as it relates to evaluating the public health risks from environmental chemical exposures.

The Emerging Issues Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. The purpose of this work group is to: (1) be a resource on the relationship between PFAS/emerging issues exposure and public health for stakeholders including: TARA, DEHS, other CDPHE divisions, other state agencies, federal agencies, and the general public; (2) increase transparency and understanding of PFAS/emerging issue data and what it means for public health;

What You Will Do

The purpose of this position is to support science communication needs for the ECHO unit. This includes translating

complex technical information into understandable information for a variety of stakeholders through appropriate

methods. In addition, this position is responsible for evaluating the effectiveness of communications to different

stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Based on guidance and support from senior TARA staff, provides risk consultation and communication expertise on environmental health problems to local public health agencies, and other stakeholders as needed.
With support of senior outreach staff, educate communities, local public health partners, and local policymakers about environmental health risks and protective measures.
With the guidance and support of other TARA staff, conduct data analysis, visualization, and interpretation to assist in data-driven decision making on environmental contaminants.
With the guidance and support of other TARA staff, conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis on the effectiveness of communication and outreach methods for different stakeholders.
Participate in responding to technical inquiries from the public (i.e., Toxcall, PFAS TAP).
Assists with public workshops, seminars and other meetings.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions Of Employment & Appeal Rights

Residency Requirement
This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

Class Code & Classification Description

I3B2T* Physical Science Researcher/Scientist I

Minimum Qualifications

Summary

The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation.

An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.

Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs.

Program Structure

Based on departmental needs, interns will be placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center and Getty Villa in Los Angeles for the first six months of their internships, and then at a Los Angeles-area museum or within a different conservation department at Getty for the second six months of the internship. Areas of focus for the internship may include American Indian collections and artifacts, conservation science, antiquities, sculpture and decorative arts, works on paper, photographs, or books.

For the second six months of the internship, placements have been previously offered at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures; the Huntington; the Fowler Museum at UCLA; the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA); and the Autry Museum of the American West.

About The Job

We have a vacancy for a researcher at the Department of Psychology in the research group for Citizens, Environment and Safety for 2 years.

The Position Combines Work In Three Externally Funded Projects

The HARMONI project aims to develop a comprehensive knowledge toolbox for hybrid products that combine the benefits of cultivated and plant-based meat alternatives, enabling the creation of appealing new food concepts and expanding future food choices. To achieve this, HARMONI brings together a consortium of Cellular Agriculture and Bioprocess Engineering (Technical University of Munich), Meat Science, Cultivated Muscle Cells and Nutrition (Aarhus University), Material Science and Microbial Systems (Katholieke Universiteit Leuven), Sustainable Food Systems (University of Helsinki), and Environmental and Consumer Psychology (NTNU), complemented by leading industrial partners. The part of NTNU is to study consumer perceptions of such products with focus group interviews, experiments and surveys. Data is likely collected in Norway, Germany, Belgium, and Finnland.
The cells4energy project is a real-world laboratory for 100% renewable energy systems. At its core lies the systemic energy cell approach, where locally generated renewable energy is intelligently stored, utilized, and interconnected with other cells. Through digital technologies and innovative business models, we test in real-world environments how a flexible, resilient, and scalable energy supply can be achieved for the future. The task for NTNU in this project is to implement and analyse the results from an automatized internet-based intervention platform to motivate energy saving. Data will be collected in Austria.
The SaferClay project is a research project focusing on developing methods to assess changes in quick clay landslide risk with time. SAFERCLAY will provide a new approach for adapted and sustainable risk management for living and building in quick clay areas, including recommendations to ensure both public and environmental safety. NTNUs task in this project is analysing perceptions of quick clay and its effects on behaviour in different stakeholder groups. A survey has been designed and is currently implemented in Norway.

What binds the work in all three projects together is the focus on collecting citizen / stakeholder perceptions on novel products, risk factors, and behaviour interventions. In all three projects, these will primarily be studied with quantitative methods, thus excellent knowledge of quantitative analysis methods, data curation and handling, as well as designing research and surveys is essential.

Your immediate leader is the head of department.

Duties of the position

Designing surveys, experiments and qualitative interviews with the respective project groups
Implementation of data collections (in cells4energy coordinated with an external technology provider for the internet platform)
Data cleaning and curation
Data analyses (mainly quantitative, but also qualitatitve)
Preparation of research papers based on the analyses
Feedback and coordination with the research partners

Required Selection Criteria

A finished degree or PhD in psychology with a specialization in environmental psychology, social psychology, behavioural psychology or closely related fields
Excellent skills in data management, curation and complex statistical analysis (e.g. structural equation modelling)
Experience in empirical work in the field
Good written and oral English skills

Preferred Selection Criteria

Experience with work in interdisciplinary fields
Experience with project management
Ability to communicate in at least one of the languages data in the different projects will be collected in (Norwegian, German, Finnish, Flemish, French) in addition to English
Experience with qualitative work

Personal characteristics

Flexibility
Ability to structure your work and handle three projects at the same time
Openness for collaboration with other disciplines and practice partners

We offer

exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment
an open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues
favourable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
employee benefits

Salary and conditions

As a researcher (code 1109) you are normally paid from gross NOK 633 400 per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The position is subject to external funding.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU.

After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

About The Application

Your application and supporting documentation must be in English.

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note:
the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your Application Must Include

CV, diplomas, and certificates
A motivation letter (max 2 pages) outlining your motivation and fit for the position
Academic works – published or unpublished – that you wish to be considered during assessment of your application (up to 5 items)
A description of the scientific/artistic works you consider most relevant, which you particularly wish to be factored into the assessment
A complete publication list
Details of projects for which you have served as project manager or had a significant position in, including information on financing, duration, and scope
Names and contact information for three relevant referees

It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for documentation of your competence.

Joint work will also be considered. If it is difficult to identify your specific input to a joint project, you must include evidence of your contributions.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

NTNU is obliged by the evaluation criteria for research quality in accordance with The San Fransisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and The obligations in the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment ( CoARA) on responsible assessment of research and recognition of a wider range of academic contributions to science and society. This means that we will pay particular attention to the quality and academic range demonstrated by your scientific work to date. We will also pay attention to research leadership and participation in research projects. Your scientific work from the last five years will be given the most weight.

Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview.

General information

Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality.

Summary

The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation.

An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.

Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs.

Program Structure

Based on departmental needs, interns will be placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center and Getty Villa in Los Angeles for the first six months of their internships, and then at a Los Angeles-area museum or within a different conservation department at Getty for the second six months of the internship. Areas of focus for the internship may include American Indian collections and artifacts, conservation science, antiquities, sculpture and decorative arts, works on paper, photographs, or books.

For the second six months of the internship, placements have been previously offered at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures; the Huntington; the Fowler Museum at UCLA; the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA); and the Autry Museum of the American West.

$45,500, plus $1,500 towards relocation expenses to Los Angeles and an additional $4,000 towards educational reimbursements, certificate courses in conservation, domestic conservation conference attendance, or other professional-development opportunities related to the internship.

Bachelor's degree in Planning, Environmental Science, or a related field.
2+ years of experience as a NEPA Analyst supporting transportation infrastructure projects.
Understanding of the NEPA process and relevant state DOT environmental procedures
Strong working knowledge of NEPA and applicable environmental regulations, including Section 4(f), Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, and other relevant environmental requirements
Familiarity with the development and management of project scopes, schedules, and budgets
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and ability to work collaboratively

Experience with developing and implementing public and stakeholder engagement strategies.
